reason: The cited evidence supports that laser cladding produces well-bonded, dense coatings (E2, E3) and that RHEA coatings on TC4 can contain intermetallics (E1), but none of the passages mention severe lattice distortion, solid-solution strengthening, finely dispersed intermetallics, or the specific TiMoNbTa composition, nor do they provide evidence that substrate ductility and corrosion resistance are preserved.
premises: Laser cladding can produce a homogeneous, fine-grained RHEA coating with strong metallurgical bonding to TC4
RHEA coatings on titanium alloys exhibit severe lattice distortion and solid-solution strengthening
RHEA coatings can contain finely dispersed intermetallic phases that provide dispersion strengthening
The combination of solid-solution and dispersion strengthening in RHEA coatings significantly increases hardness and wear resistance
The proposed TiMoNbTa-based RHEA coating will preserve TC4's beneficial properties (ductility, corrosion resistance)
